notes.title: Toxic Crusaders Launching on December 4, 2025!
notes.content: [h3]As announced at San Diego Comic Con this past weekend, we are excited to reveal the launch date for [i]Toxic Crusaders[/i]: [b]December 4th, 2025[/b]![/h3][h3][/h3][h3]Check out the Toxic Crusaders Release Date Trailer here![/h3][p][dynamiclink href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FeDPCWurjdE"][/dynamiclink][/p][h3]We understand that the change in release date/time has been pushed back multiple times by this point, but we will finally be ready to launch [i]Toxic Crusaders[/i] this December! This new release date also falls in line with the release of the new [i]The Toxic Avenger[/i] movie by Troma and Cineverse![/h3][h3][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/ddd4881269b841fae392ec2df5fe208279bc1977.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]We've been hard at work getting levels in order, fine-tuning enemies and bosses, and ensuring our Tag In/Tag Out System and RAD Mode are functioning as we intend them to. The game will also have a new player UI that should function completely different than what's currently in the demo.[/h3][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/bf89a885359889c6521bcbb28232fe90451cd697.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]Changes to game release dates are always frustrating, but our priority is releasing [i]Toxic Crusaders[/i] at the level of quality our community deserves and will enjoy.[/h3][h3][/h3][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/d5c0eb9552b67451115a86bd4c5eeeca803925bd.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]We thank you for your continued patience as we get [i]Toxic Crusaders[/i] over the finish line![/h3][h3][/h3][h3]Be sure to follow Retroware's developer page to stay up-to-date on all our games, news, and more![/h3][h3][/h3][h3][url="https://store.steampowered.com/developer/Retroware"]Steam Developer: Retroware[/url][/h3]

notes.title: “Begin the Invasion!”
notes.content:
Radiation Rangers come in all ranks and color schemes...and different mechanics. Square up against these pollution-happy thugs in the Toxic Crusaders demo!

Common Radiation Rangers don a yellow suit with some hints of green, purple, and blue throughout. These guys are eager to get the contamination going and won’t hesitate to get into your face and punch you with a fistful of PAIN!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/1dd7ac999ad9d230ac622b20f454531850b0b926.gif[/img]

Now, alone, one Radiation Ranger isn’t enough to take down a fully experienced, highly (self-proclaimed) trained Toxic Crusader. But in greater numbers, these common enemies are sure to be a threat!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/d251fc3c0257c6e09c1080f879d02070ca9c946b.gif[/img]

Speed Rangers are specially trained Radiation Rangers whose specialties specialize in KICKING! Indeed, a kick to the face will surely knock some spatial awareness into anyone distracted by the heat of battle, especially in a crowded area! So, note to self: watch out for those green Rangers!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/4a88840599f098fc977919f0862209a30d7a7bf5.gif[/img]

Burning Rangers are mid-range units that will incinerate anyone dumb enough to stand in front of them–and the glory of Smogula! You can bait them into using their flamethrowers, then run behind them to get that DE-LICIOUS combo counter going!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/2826d1ef61d1b3796c0ee50236de5eb8cf7cb42f.gif[/img]

Download and play the Toxic Crusaders demo and get a taste at what’s to come! We’ll be continuing with development in the meantime, so stay tuned for even more updates!

notes.title: Grabbin’ Some Grub!
notes.content:
When battling against Dr. Killemoff’s army of Radiation Rangers, a Toxic Crusader must always ensure their appetites are fully sated! That’s why it’s important to pick up food items as you make your way through the battlefield.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/4888ef2756edccafbe33dbd75420bd79ab4ad962.png[/img]
Eating food items satisfies your hunger–signified by their ability to restore health! However, you’ll find that every food item will have a different amount of health to give! For instance, apples will give less health than a chicken wing on a plate!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/1ef35d315ba510138adc8609cc5f90d606e5d57d.gif[/img]
And you can find food items in even the most unusual places–like after lifting up a garbage can, a mailbox, or even a fire hydrant! But no matter how they appear, you’ll always wanna grab some grub to fight off hunger and replenish that health! 

Let’s not be picky with WHERE we find our food now!

notes.title: Where’s My Car?!
notes.content:
See, everyone automatically THINKS cars are meant for nothing more than driving from Point A to Point B. But that’s everyone’s problem!

Luckily, the Toxic Crusaders know exactly how to use cars when Tromaville falls under attack by Dr. Killemoff’s Radiation Rangers, or if any local thugs join in on the rampage!

THROWING CARS!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/aad32cdfefbfd0ee11312d89efc0a6a8d8055486.png[/img]

When it comes to another one of Dr. Killemoff’s schemes, the Toxic Crusaders must use every weapon, ability, and…parked car they can find to drive back the evil forces of pollution!

That said, you’d best make sure your car is parked inside your garage, or maybe even parked on your driveway, because if it’s out on the street–uh, well, consider it to be a potential contribution to the noble cause of fighting pollution!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/2f83b8506bc924d5e61698af76d9628a41e951b9.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/ba938697c7b0cd9e35fa7898846604f49a316d04.gif[/img]

But when the fighting finds its way to the Tromaville junkyard…all bets are off. No Toxic Crusader would ever have any second thoughts of tossing a rusty, damaged car at a bunch of Radiation Rangers! How’s THAT for crowd control?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/a0a63b8f7e7b908939744dadc38d1ca757e59c6a.png[/img]
Whether it’s beating up Dr. Killemoff’s minions, or teaching the local thugs a lesson, you can count on the Toxic Crusaders to use any parked car to defend themselves and the home they love!

Keep your eyes peeled for even more!

notes.title: Likeness to the Figures #5 - Headbanger
notes.content:
Coming off the heels of joining the Toxic Crusaders as a former henchman of Dr. Killemoff is Headbanger! But what sets his modern in-game design from his crazy-looking original action figure? Let’s take a look!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/f0da24d5b759b79350136bd6ac77412a5a0be39b.png[/img]

Headbanger’s action figure from the early 90’s was certainly a sight for sore eyes–or perhaps…it helped CAUSE sore eyes?? Either way, we can clearly see how Dr. Bender and surf boy Fender were conjoined together into one “hideously deformed creature of superhuman size and strength!

Taking Dr. Bender’s brains and Fender’s brawn, the action figure showed off the former’s scientific lab look–with an orange bowtie and some writing utensils to boot–along with the latter’s laid back, casual appearance–not to mention the sporting of his muscular physique!

As for Headbanger’s in-game design…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/4d4f298e2b201d66c8ecd14186bbbce742ab58c6.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/81495a38704720538f342bf930bb66422cdd6b93.jpg[/img]

By comparison, we can clearly see the extreme lack of ORANGE–with green splotches of goo (Magoop?) on the shirt and Dr. Bender’s pants for the sprite design, while being more prolific in the comic cutscene design. A chain also runs diagonally along where the two former individuals are now joined as one! 

To draw Headbanger’s in-game appearance even closer to the original cartoon, we can see that Dr. Fender loses those orange glasses that were present on the action figure–which is fine, since he won’t need them to take on Dr. Killemoff’s Radiation Rangers anyway!

No matter the foe, you can always count on Headbanger to with the smartest and most laid back plan ever!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/d251fc3c0257c6e09c1080f879d02070ca9c946b.gif[/img]

notes.title: Frank Strikes Back!
notes.content:
Bursting onto the scene inside the restaurant, Frank is ready to take on the Toxic Crusaders with his dangerous melee attacks!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/69d9aae21d18d1a3c7340074d6de6539e4b9b6da.gif[/img]
As a reference to the character who lost his arm to Toxie in the movie, The Toxic Avenger, Frank always poses with one arm behind his back–not to mention that he uses one arm at a time (based on whichever side he’s facing) to deliver punches!

And you’ll want to keep your distance if you knock him down! Like other enemies, Frank will perform a “wake up” attack by kicking into the air with his legs to regain his footing!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/21c327aa427534c0203d3abc61e4e5e2fe1f6988.gif[/img]
Not only can Frank punish players for trying to spam attack him as soon as he gets back up, he’ll brace his active arm to block ALL normal attacks! However, you can still hurt him by using a dash attack or a special attack!

notes.title: Working Out With…Enemies?!
notes.content:
[b]NOTE: All screenshots in this post feature in-game levels that are still in development. Their final designs may differ from what is shown.[/b]

As the Toxic Crusaders endeavor to clean the streets of Tromaville from all that is evil and foul, they’ll have to clean up the Health Club, too! You’ll find even the thugs of Tromaville working out (or at least appearing to) at the Health Club–all of them sporting new outfits! Take a look at their level-specific designs in-game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/e0476e51678c327853e4b2413bc5a7168ddb4d25.png[/img]
You’ll find Ricos spinning nunchucks, while donning light exercise clothes, and Leroys (still armed with their knives) wearing purple and blue pants and sweaters! Both enemies will be wearing headbands, and both will still wanna knock out any Toxic Crusaders dumb enough to disturb their time in the gym!

Crashing their way onto the scene from our MAGFest 2024 demo is Headbanger–an accidental creation formed by combining both Dr. Bender and delivery boy Fender into one person! Merging both brains and brawn, Headbanger is ready to join the battle against the extraterrestrial Smogulans!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/81495a38704720538f342bf930bb66422cdd6b93.jpg[/img]
Similar to the original action figure, Fender’s side retains his blue shirt and armband. His necklace color is now purple, and his red sandal has been changed to a flip flop. Also, the design on his shorts was changed to be mostly yellow with green palm tree tops, compared to the figure’s largely inverse design.

As for Dr. Bender’s side, he still retains his white lab shirt, but his in-game design ditches those orange glasses and bowtie on his figure. Also, much of his side has color-swapped parts, such as the pens being individually colored instead of just orange, his pants are now purple and his belt is black, and his lab glove is yellow instead of white! Lastly, his shoe has also changed to have a greenish hue instead of being orange!

[h3][b]Punch, Smack, & Headbutt![/b][/h3]

Holding a flask of Magoop in his hand, Dr. Bender crashes it onto the ground to cause a chemical explosion that damages all enemies around himself and Fender!

No doubt Yvonne is a talented singer–always lifting the spirits of the team throughout the original cartoon and celebrating with them after a well-fought victory! We just had to include her singing in some capacity in the game, so we decided to make her unquestionable talent her  special attack!

Dr. Killemoff and his Radiation Rangers descend upon Tromaville in their Apocalypse Attackcopters! Inspired by several scenes in the cartoon, we thought it would be neat to bring back these Smogulan flying machines of...smog! Don't miss them in the opening cutscene of the demo!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/98140bd1c94deceaf4a49f064a2c42c803199cfb.png[/img]

His all-too-familiar sneezes sent Dr. Killemoff and his Radiation Rangers soaring into the air in cartoon, but now we've contained his sneezes into an AOE attack that can knock down enemies surrounding the former ace pilot!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/94e0ea5479319fc83cb4c9f6f08f24a815660d41.png[/img]
[h3][b]4. Home is Where the Junkyard Is![/b][/h3]
In the last section of the demo, vigilant players will be able to spot the tattered makeshift home of the Toxic Crusaders in the background! From its humble beginnings when Toxie founded the team with Nozone and Major Disaster, to its current state in the demo, any fan of the 90s cartoon should easily notice the HQ of the Toxic Crusaders!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/94b1716032d3f4dde460c98abce0739bc2983037.png[/img]

notes.title: Likeness to the Figures #4 - Radiation Ranger
notes.content:
The most common unit in the Smogulan army takes center stage in this week’s Likeness to the Figures comparison! Check out the similarities (and differences) between this enemy’s in-game sprite and its classic action figure!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/1ecdaa60b6a97ad27b0713b8cb046d1f61afe151.png[/img]
[h3][b]1. “Radiation Rangers, Front and Center!”[/b][/h3]

While the figure has this green, blue, and orange chest unit (likely for breathing in only SMOG!), the in-game Radiation Rangers have been outfitted with updated suits allowing for greater mobility (and so we can see that HUGE radiation icon!). Plus, we tossed out the orange goggles for sweet purple ones!

You might also notice the radiation icons on the sides of the shoulders are also lacking any orange on the in-game sprite. Oh, and we ditched the orange strap running down the upper arm, too!

notes.title: Dev Log #1 - Journey to Working on Toxic Crusaders
notes.content:
Get to know the lead game developer behind Toxic Crusaders–Sam!

[h2][b]1. Please briefly describe your journey as a game developer and how you came to work on Toxic Crusaders.[/b][/h2]

[b]Sam[/b]: I've been making games as long as I can remember! When I was a kid, my Dad gave me an Acorn Electron computer, and with it was a book on how to write games in BASIC. I'd type up the code from that book and change/mod the games to my liking! Then as a teenager I made fan games and some original games in The Games Factory and uploaded them to an old GeoCities website. It was only when I started college that I didn't have the time anymore, but when the indie game renaissance happened I jumped straight back in and started making games commercially, and had enough successes that I could quit my job and make games for a living, especially after making the first Angry Video Game Nerd game, which gave me a headstart.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/b4ee5c088b85118196a8136bd1cd4846b2596a11.gif[/img]
[b]Sam[/b]: I was given the honor of developing Toxic Crusaders by the guys at Retroware after the success of Angry Video Game Nerd I & II Deluxe. Ryan, the president of Retroware, wanted me to be the one who did it, and I am eternally grateful for the opportunity! It's been tough, and there have been ups and downs, but what we are making is getting better and more exciting every day.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/0bb7324691f427f68b89f627a0d4a5881a82241d.png[/img]
[h2][b]2. Have you heard of the Toxic Crusaders and/or Troma prior to working on the game? What value do you think referring to the source material has while developing this kind of title?[/b][/h2]

[b]Sam[/b]: Yes! As a kid I liked the cartoon and had some of the toys, and as an adult I am big into horror and B-movies, so I have also been a Toxic Avenger and TROMA fan for a good while.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/4d5bc84d6c2514ba816a12197db4e2a5db73d693.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/ebb5a8f02767d698df3221dc38dcc0bf36ec1407.png[/img]
[b]Sam[/b]: Funny story - I had a memory of Toxic Crusaders, and was a Toxic Avenger fan, but I didn't put two and two together and realize they were the same thing until the AVGN episode came along. It was a real "idiotic eureka moment" for me.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/6a7b68be55d991bb0fec85e7988b251374d81a52.png[/img]
[h2][b]3. What is it like developing a beat-em-up game? What do you think makes Toxic Crusaders stand out from similar titles today? Thirdly, can you describe what you think is the appeal of beat-em-ups compared to other genres?[/b][/h2]

[b]Sam[/b]: The guys at Retroware gave me the opportunity to bring in some expert help, so I enlisted Mentski, the most clued-up guy I know on the subject, to consult. He wrote an extensive study on the classic Beat-Em-Ups and what makes them work, plus what makes a lot of the modern ones not work. Game feel is key, we spent a huge amount of time getting the exact right frame-perfect feel and sound, because the genre is all about that catharsis and satisfaction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/54436fc962d5a51b171fe80e13dc793557377e94.gif[/img]
[b]Sam[/b]: Beat-Em-Ups are such a release. Where I have previously mostly worked with platform games with an emphasis on challenge, for Toxic Crusaders we really focused on making something that makes you feel good to play. Not that the game isn't challenging, but many modern Beat-Em-Ups miss the point with big difficulty spikes and frustration.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/e9c4c1abe6fa355dc56ba6ed8ba3ea668843b5bf.png[/img]
[h2][b]4. While Toxic Crusaders is still undergoing development, what are some things that you thought were fun and/or interesting to implement into the game?[/b][/h2]

[b]Sam[/b]: Something Toxic Crusaders has over other cartoons of the time is its wicked sense of humor. Where other popular cartoon teams often just had a change of color and weapons and personality traits, the Toxic Crusaders are all unique and very different to one another. That means we spent a lot of time making the characters feel and play differently, with unique animations and stats, with so much personality in all of their moves.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/b943c8a032b30e1a4383613502ccff2c89dac064.gif[/img]
[h2][b]5. As a game developer, what do you want players to take away after playing Toxic Crusaders?[/b][/h2]

[b]Sam[/b]: When the Twin Peaks revival came out a few years back, I was going through a pretty rough time, as was the world, and I remember watching the first episode and being hit with this awesome, warm feeling and thinking "I am so, so happy that this is back." Seeing the show and its characters return, brought up to date without losing what made it special, made me feel happy, even when I wasn't even watching it, it's like it reawakened that '90s spirit for me. It wasn't just "Hey guys, remember this?", it also gave me the same feeling the show did back in the day, but as for my modern self.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/92b6ee2b63f548ef39e62ac6cb0c7365cb92d5b9.png[/img]
[b]Sam[/b]: That's what I want people to feel when they play this. Not just "Hey, I remember this cartoon and this genre of game," there are plenty of those. I want Toxie to fill people with that spirit and humor. Toxie and friends fight to save the environment from those who destroy it for their own personal gain, and today that is more relevant than ever. No matter how hopeless things may seem, Toxie and friends will always do what's right, will always have hope, and will always see the funny side.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/7f85c9d739fcb6551a070a206c2e08f6ccaaf556.png[/img]
[b]Sam[/b]: I hope that beating up a bunch of polluters brings great catharsis, I hope that Toxie's bright and inspiring attitude reminds people to have hope, and I hope that this crazy team of oddballs can keep you laughing until the day we eventually save the world for real.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/a72f87e9b9dd17fa8780e8cdab274774a1a195eb.png[/img]

notes.title: Development Progression Through Art: Backgrounds
notes.content:
There’s always more to game development than just designing characters, attack patterns, and enemy behavior. Creating the backgrounds takes just as much careful planning and execution!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/b943c8a032b30e1a4383613502ccff2c89dac064.gif[/img]
[h3][b]Detailing from the Original Cartoon[/b][/h3]
There’s no question that we had to take inspiration directly from the original Toxic Crusaders cartoon! Here’s one of the reference sheets our art director made that breaks down some of the Tromaville environments from the first episode!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/109a7e86e08d349f66ebcf76d2428c770f1edc9b.png[/img]
We wanted fans of the cartoon to notice our not-so-secret nods to scenes that may look all too familiar in-game!

[h3][b]Concept Art[/b][/h3]
After pointing out what references will be used, our art director then communicates what we need to Jeff Delgado, another artist on the team, and he provides concept art of what the final design could look like.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/6a762317fbc2c0bd2a618920e7c72c4a1d9eec5e.png[/img]
[h3][b]Initial Renditions[/b][/h3]
Following this, we then have our pixel artists build out the assets for the level based on the artwork. Something to note here: it isn’t 1-to-1 with the concept art, but it serves as a critical guide to fleshing out the actual level. This is also the stage where we implement a player-character sprite–like Toxie!--into the level rendition to get an idea of how they would look against the background.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/e4632d93f7048f85b9b98afa09e6fd603ab7ae72.png[/img]
[h3][b]Final Design and Implementation[/b][/h3]
Lastly, once theartists complete the background, and after it’s been checked over by our art director, the entire piece is implemented into the game and ready for playtesting–and, ya know, regular playing!

(Note: the above “army” of Radiation Rangers comes from a testing build of the game and DOES NOT represent an actual part of a level in-game)

First off, here’s some concept art of the common Smogulan enemy drawn by our Art Director, Xander Arnot!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/6c303212a9ac9716f2260c1cdf30cb5e151edbf3.jpg[/img]
Alone, a single Radiation Ranger isn’t much of a threat, since, in terms of the game, regular Radiation Rangers can only throw punches–albeit very consistently and in quick succession!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/f00ac1d71fc5569c935652fae7b09463f978180b.png[/img]
Rarely will you find a Radiation Ranger on their own! It’s all about strength in numbers! And if there’s too many “Rad” Rangers to boot, even a Toxic Crusader may find themselves in a heap of trouble!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/4a88053c7082eff30a99dd52aa39a3c309d3525f.png[/img]
[h3][b]Polluting the City, One Grossolium Barrel at a Time![/b][/h3]
Not only can Radiation Rangers throw hands, they can also throw Grossolium barrels! These vats of toxic waste are freshly deployed from Dr. Killemoff’s forces, and, when hitting the ground, they’ll release the Grossolium stored within. If you’re a normal civilian, RUN AWAY! But if you’re a Toxic Crusader, there’s nothing to fear! Standing on top of the spilled Grossolium will increase your “Rad Meter,” which can help you activate “Rad Mode” faster to dish out even more pain against the Smogulan grunts!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/e4756a7aa6ff07a86033775f7645f61554c7f347.gif[/img]
[h3][b]Supporting Their Superiors![/b][/h3]
You’ll also find normal Radiation Rangers supporting higher ranked Smogulan forces, such as the likes of Speed (SPD) Rangers and Burning Rangers! That said, it’s recommended you take down the normal Radiation Rangers first before tackling their superiors!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/871cbd4b234ed9bad863b7575ebd655416dd59d9.png[/img]

notes.title: "Forward! MARCH!" - Toxic Crusaders Concept Art #4
notes.content:
Up next for our character features is the best soldier Mother Nature has fighting for her–Major Disaster!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/54436fc962d5a51b171fe80e13dc793557377e94.gif[/img]
[h3][b]Concept Art[/b][/h3]

Taking inspiration from the original Toxic Crusaders cartoon, Major Disaster’s in-game design has taken on a similar appearance with a modern spin. Take a look at Major Disaster’s amazing concept art drawn by comic artist Steve Gregson:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/9a6230a22007f538b9082e4f6b37e3614f10462c.jpg[/img]
And here's another concept art piece drawn by our Art Director, Xander Arnot:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/7284b83906efb3b02bf2475bd9a9727378e90a3c.png[/img]
[h3][b]Weapons of the Natural Kind![/b][/h3]

We wanted to give Major Disaster the raw power of Mother Nature! Speaking of stomping power, players will notice that whenever Major Disaster runs, the ground will shake! (Screen Shake can be disabled in the Options menu)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/cfa3e8021a21d794d0291d989b0553b212bcc1d9.gif[/img]
Along with his innate strength, Major Disaster employs a host of natural weapons at his disposal! His dash attack features a tree branch armblade, while his back attack causes vines and more branches to sprout from behind!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/6ba7f33930ca4d5735450b9f19688b314801d3a5.png[/img]
Finally, for his special attack, Major Disaster can summon a group of large vines from underground for massive AOE damage! While this special attack is quite powerful, it should be noted that the Major is vulnerable in the animation frames after the vines go away, so be cautious!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/281ffab5d22344262b91ed04eef18c46052c5841.gif[/img]
[h3][b]In-Game Design[/b][/h3]

Even when he’s idle, Major Disaster’s pose is all the more intimidating to the Smogulan forces and their allies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/497ec07bf4769cf9238c196da9762e48d4c5ee26.png[/img]
In addition, when it comes to jump attacks, one of the Major’s moves is a heavy kick-down, which can stun enemies for a follow-up combo attack!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/764a1867dc0a26847245aea90168aa119689fe4e.png[/img]
With great power comes a slower speed. While Major Disaster is strong up close, he lacks speed when walking and running. Even with his Rad Mode active, the Major Disaster’s power greatly increases, but his speed is still miles below other characters.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/99f0d1feba24a8d14c6e8b0f6433f7375404d90d.png[/img]
Despite his slow movement speed, Major Disaster is both a vital and powerful member of the Toxic Crusaders! With Mother Nature at his command, nothing will stop the Major from dishing out destruction against the forces of Smogula!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/054831d1e14a0a3c5c2b14bea076c4096c6383a7.png[/img]

notes.title: Giving Life to the Story - Comic Book Cutscenes
notes.content:
Did you know [i]Toxic Crusaders[/i] used to have a comic book series? We wanted to incorporate the spirit of that piece of Toxie history into the game via motion comics!

[h3][b]Concepting Out Comic Cutscenes[/b][/h3]

We wanted to drive the story of the game via comic cutscenes as a direct reference to the original comic runs of the Toxic Crusaders in the early 90s. 

Artist Steve Gregson drew up sketches for all of the motion comics players will be able to see in-game! Check out some of the panels he worked on below, going from concept sketch to final design:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/80c607dbf2268664a1d52fd8dfd05116d5751744.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/1557932da3956f050cf05289b646cf5598c49d13.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/226a724e556ca099ef932fba2eabce529a54e9e0.gif[/img]
[h3][b]Continuing After Many Years–I Mean, Days![/b][/h3]
It’s no question we wanted [i]Toxic Crusaders[/i] to act as “the Season 2 that we never got” from the original cartoon. This was an important fact that we wanted to highlight, so much so that we even have some of the in-game characters–in true 4th wall-breaking fashion–make direct nods to this continuity between the game and the cartoon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/7f85c9d739fcb6551a070a206c2e08f6ccaaf556.png[/img]
[h3][b]Bringing (Back) Personality[/b][/h3]
We’re delighted to be working with TeamFourStar, who are providing all of the voiceover lines for each character! We’ll go into more detail on our team-up with them at a later date, but, for now, it’s comics, in-game comics, and motion comics galore!

notes.title: “The Name’s Junkyard!” - Toxic Crusaders Concept Art #3
notes.content:
Coming up next on our character spotlight pipeline is none other than Junkyard, the coolest, good-est canine companion any Toxic Crusader could ask for!

[h3][b]Concept Art[/b][/h3]

Without a doubt we took loads of inspiration from his appearance in the Toxic Crusaders cartoon, but we also had a vision for giving Junkyard a modernized look to his original appearance. Here, we have some wonderful concept art of Junkyard drawn by UK comic artist Steve Gregson:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/e218da4cfdabcdba8f368ba24174e9e1c9a38558.jpg[/img]
[h3][b]Taking Swipes, Howling with Fright![/b][/h3]

When creating Junkyard’s in-game sprite and animations, we wanted to make sure he would create as much lovable havoc as possible. In the original cartoon, Junkyard certainly presented himself as a polite fellow when we first met him, but in the game, he becomes a formidable Crusader that can swipe, spin, and bite away at Dr. Killemoff’s Radiation Rangers!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/f84bc7ed3e6899e2cbbc3fb662a02b077d950db1.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/b4ee5c088b85118196a8136bd1cd4846b2596a11.gif[/img]

notes.title: Enemy Spotlight: Burning Rangers
notes.content:
It's been a while (or has it?) since we last saw any combat engagements involving the Smogulan army, and it looks they've made A LOT of progress in building up their forces anew! As one of the latest additions among Dr. Killemoff's Radiation Ranger army, the Burning Rangers are here to turn up the heat!

[h3][b]Concept Art[/b][/h3]
We had loads of fun designing a host of new enemies, and the Burning Ranger was certainly one of them! Here’s a look at some of the concept art drawn by our Art Director, Xander Arnot, to get an idea of how this enemy unit would look like:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/d4fc3be5d820e376a9a8114da6d0e0efc7eac114.png[/img]
[h3][b]Place Among the Smogulan Forces![/b][/h3]
Burning Rangers possess a similar helmet to those seen on normal Radiation Rangers. However, unlike their regular counterparts, Burning Rangers are equipped with fuel tanks connected to their Flamethrowers. These weapons can shoot out bursts of fire in a straight path in front of the Burning Ranger, limiting them to a close and somewhat medium range.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/34f321096e6b76223b16c869de8fb78ee32ef6f1.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/5f26563beae6551a38760ba5af12dcc9222d56ba.png[/img]
Burning Rangers also have noticeably more health than regular Radiation Rangers, so be prepared to bring the pain against them as soon as they appear! Something else to note: When using their Flamethrowers, Burning Rangers will always fire in a linear, horizontal direction at players who are both close enough and on the same plane as them!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/b77bf8501ac1ef7d36ad292e9d9e825c027d865e.png[/img]
[h3][b]Final Design[/b][/h3]
Burning Rangers are adorned with tactical Smogulan gear and are easily identifiable by their red operation jackets and warmly-colored Flamethrowers. Players can think of Burning Rangers as an enemy level a step above the green Speed (SPD) Rangers, so they're definitely a formidable force! As some of the newest units out of the Radiation Ranger army, we hope players will enjoy taking on these enemies exclusive to the game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/91c361c08710416463b5d9c920423abc5abf1666.png[/img]
We're excited to share more as we continue with development! Stick around for more updates soon!

notes.title: References to the Toxic Avenger Movie!
notes.content:
It’s no secret the original [i]Toxic Crusaders[/i] cartoon was based on the live-action Toxic Avenger movie, so we just had to pack in references to it, too!

First up, we’ve got the kid with bandages on his head riding a bike at the very start of the demo level, which is a direct reference to the kid seen in [i]The Toxic Avenger[/i] as he’s traveling down a road!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/7b7d700d84e8e8cc71c8af685c33775b704193cf.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/b3b2e787d2ec7fca1864579095893ccf284ba88c.png[/img]
Next, we’ve got the very noticeable reference to the exterior look of “The Mexican Place” as seen in the original movie!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/e7173582aba1f1f06378ad127611e07c0c231896.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/ffd9813c5ad80ca1ba2892132c15d8d0ad751636.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/e4545f438dbabe999625329e117fc236b6f30ff1.png[/img]
Now, for those of you who’ve seen the film, the common mob enemies running around here should evoke some nostalgia.

Here’s a look (from left to right) at Rico, Leroy, and Frank from the scene just before they throw hands with Toxie himself!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/4d5bc84d6c2514ba816a12197db4e2a5db73d693.png[/img]
Below, the positions of the characters are different, where we have Leroy, Frank, and Rico in that order, instead:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/ebb5a8f02767d698df3221dc38dcc0bf36ec1407.png[/img]
For Frank, we gave an extra reference to his ultimate fate in [i]The Toxic Avenger[/i], where he met a very…graphic fate that isn’t (unfortunately?) present in the game! However, to reflect this, we created Frank’s in-game sprite to always have an arm behind him at a lowered position–a callback to when Toxie ripped off his arm in the movie! That said, in-game Frank will always attack players with only one arm!

Thirdly, the train tracks at the start of the junkyard section are a reference to when Toxie begins his journey in the movie! When Melvin Junko first turns into Toxie, he walks along a set of train tracks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/cb9b6406030c519b5006f332391e32c48ecfcd05.jpg[/img]
And here’s where those tracks eventually “led” to in-game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/05557dfd3ac800af115d8b1be782b11f7add7fdd.png[/img]
We’ve also included the B.G. Whip mob character, who isn’t a specific character, per se, but she is merely a reference to some of the Apocalypse Inc. henchwomen from the second Toxic Avenger film.

And here we have concept art drawn by Bryce Collins for the eventual in-game sprite:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/7aecf1c07d64d89249395dfb7c6ef0c2f6a7c4bc.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/055520032fb2bd6e87a6d81aaa107dac668369fa.png[/img]

notes.title: "Here, How's This?" - Toxic Crusaders Concept Art #2

In the original cartoon, Yvonne took a mostly supportive role to the team, boosting their morale with one of her songs or giving conveniently helpful advice to her boyfriend, Toxie. This time around, as the game is a "continuation" of the original cartoon, we wanted to have Yvonne join the fray as a playable character and now an official member of the team!

To start things off, we’ve got images in the order of Yvonne from the original cartoon, Claire from [i]The Toxic Avenger: Part II[/i], and Sarah from [i]Citizen Toxie: The Toxic Avenger IV[/i]. The idea was to combine elements from all iterations of Toxie’s girlfriend into the Yvonne we see in this game!

[u][b]From Generic Default to…COLORS EVERYWHERE![/b][/u]
When we began development, we didn’t even think about giving each character a unique color for their attacks. At the start, every character just had a generic, dull-looking impact effect that was shared with enemy sprites!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/24aba59439b8de86defbb2066b9b6b14a7b206ed.png[/img]
But then we realized how much cooler everyone would look if we splashed some color into their punches, kicks, and every other attack! Thus…

[u][b]Colors Across the Board[/b][/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/7ab58ce15df1e2a600f1265a53496610e12a703f.png[/img]
We essentially picked out colors from each character’s in-game design. Coupling that with a “glowing” impact effect led to very satisfying results! Now each character could look cool, while giving their respective players an indication on whether they’re leaving an [b]IMPACT [/b]or not!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/e9c4c1abe6fa355dc56ba6ed8ba3ea668843b5bf.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/0bb7324691f427f68b89f627a0d4a5881a82241d.png[/img]
[u][b]Streets and Restaurants Bursting with Color![/b][/u]
Seeing the maximum of four players on-screen at once really shows how beautifully chaotic things can get, especially seeing all the bursts of color throughout! Playing as Major Disaster? Smack ‘em with red! Playing as Yvonne? Kick ‘em with pink! Playing as Nozone? Soar down in blue!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/6a7b68be55d991bb0fec85e7988b251374d81a52.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43799837/be4e7b8657882436895b2b98b713c8e42a9805c1.png[/img]
We’re excited to share more about [i]Toxic Crusaders[/i] as we move along with development!
Stick around for more updates!

notes.title: Toxic Crusaders NOW HAS Live Action Cutscenes??
notes.content:
[h1][b]Greetings, citizens of Tromaville![/b][/h1]

[h3]Here's update from the Retroware crew about our game Toxic Crusaders!![/h3]

We drove up to the Troma offices in NYC and filmed with the one and only Lloyd Kaufman. Lloyd is the President of Troma (the creators of the Toxic Avenger and the Toxic Crusaders cartoon our game is based on.) Lloyd usually intros all of their movies and shows for their physical releases... so, we thought having Lloyd introduce [i][b]the game[/b][/i] would be really fitting. So, YES, we have live action footage of Lloyd Kaufman IN Toxic Crusaders: The Game!! That is coupled with the motion comic cutscenes and FULL voice acting in the game. [i]Plus... some extra surprises coming soon![/i]

[h2]This footage will be used in the game itself as well as Steam Next Fest this June![/h2]

notes.title: 32 years later, Toxic Crusaders is getting a new beat 'em up
notes.content: Toxic Crusaders was a curious early '90s cartoon for kids, based on a schlocky, campy action film series that was emphatically not for kids. I never saw the cartoon, which possibly never aired outside of the United States, but I am familiar with The Toxic Avenger series it was based on. That series has spawned four films, and all are incredibly silly, varying levels of offensive, and often obscenely violent... Read more.
